changes.before: Make the named input inherit the form’s 20px text, use a 200px border box, and preserve label and submit-button behavior.
changes.after: Make form text readable while keeping the controls working.

before: Native form controls have browser-provided appearances and do not always inherit page typography in the way ordinary text does. Explicit font: inherit can make their text consistent while preserving their native editing and activation behavior.

font: inherit copies the parent’s computed font settings. border-box makes the declared input width include padding and border. min-height reserves room without pretending that one height fits every language or zoom setting. Keep the label association, name and button type in HTML. Do not remove native appearance or focus indicators merely to make the control look like a painted rectangle; appearance can vary across browsers.
Make the named input inherit the form’s 20px text, use a 200px border box, and preserve label and submit-button behavior.
after: Native controls are the browser’s built-in inputs and buttons. They can have different starting fonts from the page around them. You can style them while keeping their normal editing and button behavior.

`font: inherit` copies the parent’s font settings. `box-sizing: border-box` includes padding and borders in the stated width. A `min-height` gives a minimum amount of room but still lets a control grow.

Keep the input’s label, ID, and name, and keep the button’s `type="submit"`. Those HTML settings make the form work. Keep a visible focus mark too. Try the controls with a keyboard; their appearance can vary between browsers.

before.question: Does font:inherit remove the input’s editing behavior or its label association?
choices: Yes; an inherited font turns it into a paragraph.
Only if border-box is also used.
No; it changes typography, not those HTML behaviors.
before.explanation: Presentation and native control semantics are separate. Keep HTML contracts while styling readable controls.

after.question: Does font: inherit remove the input’s typing behavior or its connection to the label?
choices: Yes. It turns the input into a paragraph.
Only when border-box is also used.
No. It changes the font, not those HTML behaviors.
after.explanation: The input remains an input. Its label and editing behavior come from HTML.
